s: Which inscription mentions that Rishabhadatta deposited 2,000 Karshapanas in a guild of weavers belonging to Govardhana?
x:
The famous Nasik Inscription of Rishabhadatta (Ushavadatta) records that he deposited 2,000 Karshapanas with the guild (Shreni) of weavers at Govardhana. The interest earned from this permanent deposit was utilized for charitable and religious purposes, especially for the maintenance of Buddhist monks. This inscription is one of the strongest pieces of evidence showing that guilds functioned as banking institutions in ancient India. It also demonstrates the advanced commercial organization that existed during the Satavahana period.
Hence, the correct answer is
Option (2).

s: What is the meaning of the word "Gulmika" mentioned in the Maski (Macedonian) inscription?
x:
The term "Gulmika" referred to the head of a military-cum-administrative unit responsible for maintaining law and order in a group of villages. In APPSC history books, it is generally interpreted as a village headman/local administrative officer. The term appears in early inscriptions, including the Maski (often written as Macedonian in older question papers) inscription.
Hence, the correct answer is
Option (1).

s: Which of the following pair is incorrectly matched?
x:
The pair Nagarjuna – Buddhacharita is incorrect because Buddhacharita was written by Ashvaghosha, one of the greatest Buddhist scholars and poets of the Kushana period. Nagarjuna, on the other hand, was the founder of the Madhyamika (Middle Path) school of Mahayana Buddhism and authored important philosophical works such as Mulamadhyamaka Karika and Suhrllekha. The remaining pairs are correctly matched: • Hala – Gathasaptasati • Vatsyayana – Kamasutra • Gunadhya – Brihatkatha
Hence, the correct answer is
Option (2).

The Amatya was an important ministerial officer in the Satavahana administration. He assisted the king in matters of governance, finance, justice and general administration. The office of the Amatya was one of the highest civil positions in the kingdom. The Satavahana administrative hierarchy included officials such as: • Amatya – Minister • Mahasenapati – Commander-in-Chief • Mahabhoja – Provincial governor • Maharathi – Feudatory chief
Hence, the correct answer is
Option (1).

s: Gunadhya wrote Brihatkatha in which language?
x:
Gunadhya, one of the greatest literary figures associated with the Satavahana period, composed the famous Brihatkatha in Paishachi Prakrit, a now-extinct literary language. Although the original text has been lost, it survives through later Sanskrit adaptations such as: • Kathasaritsagara by Somadeva • Brihatkatha Manjari by Kshemendra The work greatly influenced Indian narrative literature.
Hence, the correct answer is
Option (2).
